papers.title: α5-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptors regulate state transitions in cortical networks and modulate susceptibility to epileptiform discharges.
papers.summary: This study investigated the role of α5-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in regulating cortical state transitions and epileptiform discharges. Using acute brain slices from wild-type and α5 knockout mice, the authors found that α5KO networks exhibited slower spontaneous activity and tolerance to high-amplitude spike-and-wave discharges, suggesting a critical role for α5-nAChRs in cortical excitability and ictogenesis.

papers.title: Claustral pathway coordinates distributed cortical dynamics with hippocampal output during sleep to promote memory consolidation
papers.summary: This study identifies a projection-defined claustral neuron population (CLAsc) targeting the subicular complex that is preferentially recruited during slow-wave sleep. Optogenetic activation of these neurons during post-learning sleep enhanced spatial memory consolidation and imposed a stereotyped cortical-subicular motif of gamma-rich Up states and coordinated Down states, suggesting the claustrum coordinates distributed brain states during sleep to support memory consolidation.

papers.title: Cognitive exertion reshapes resting-state EEG markers across the adult lifespan
papers.summary: This study examined the effects of cognitive exertion on resting-state EEG markers across the adult lifespan. Across multiple datasets, cognitive exertion consistently slowed individual alpha peak frequency and increased alpha power, while aperiodic shifts were age-dependent, with post-task steepening in younger adults flattening with age, indicating these EEG metrics exhibit acute state-dependency with post-task recordings offering a promising framework for indexing individual differences in ageing.

papers.title: Inkjet-Printed Aqueous Graphene Suspensions on Flexible Substrates for Multimodal Wearable Continuous Health Monitoring.
papers.summary: This paper describes the development of inkjet-printed graphene electrodes on PET substrates for wearable health monitoring. The electrodes showed high conductivity, flexibility, and reusability, and successfully recorded ECG, EEG, EOG, and EMG signals with high correlation to gel-based commercial electrodes, demonstrating potential for practical applications.

papers.title: Brain-wide reconfiguration of burst firing by psilocybin reveals 5-HT2A-dependent circuit dynamics
papers.summary: Using multi-region Neuropixels recordings in mice, this study found that psilocybin selectively reconfigured burst firing rather than mean firing rates across cortical, thalamic, and hippocampal circuits, with decreased hippocampal burst firing and bidirectional modulation in the thalamus. Most burst effects were abolished by the 5-HT2A antagonist ketanserin, indicating a 5-HT2A-dependent reconfiguration of burst coding underlying the psychedelic state.

papers.title: Predicting Anxiety Trajectories from Individual Differences in Sleep-Related Distress Alleviation
papers.summary: This cohort study investigated whether individual differences in REM sleep-related overnight distress alleviation predict anxiety recovery. In 223 adults with insomnia and psychiatric symptoms, stronger REM-related distress alleviation at baseline predicted greater anxiety improvement after two months, independent of treatment, suggesting a link between REM sleep emotion regulation and anxiety recovery.

papers.title: Low-frequency anodal transcranial pulsed current stimulation (0.5-5 Hz): effects on EEG band amplitude, interhemispheric coherence, and cognitive performance.
papers.summary: This double-blinded crossover study in 17 healthy adults examined the effects of low-frequency anodal transcranial pulsed current stimulation (tPCS) at 0.5, 1, 3, 5 Hz and sham on EEG and cognitive performance. The results showed frequency-dependent modulation of EEG coherence and power (e.g., 1 Hz increased coherence, others reduced power) but no significant changes in reaction time or error rates.

papers.title: Increased aperiodic offset and heightened alpha power characterize resting-state EEG activity in Parkinson's disease
papers.summary: This study characterized resting-state EEG in Parkinson's disease patients OFF medication versus controls, finding higher aperiodic offset and alpha power in patients, replicated across EEG systems. Aperiodic parameters scaled positively with age and disease duration, suggesting increased aperiodic offset and alpha power as robust neurophysiological markers of PD, with aperiodic parameters potentially tracking disease duration.

papers.title: Normative Modeling of EEG Complexity Reveals Cortical Rigidity Associated with Pain Severity in Chronic Pain.
papers.summary: This study applied normative modeling to EEG complexity (Higuchi fractal dimension) in chronic pain patients. Larger negative deviations from healthy norms, particularly in frontal regions, were significantly correlated with higher pain intensity, suggesting that normative deviation mapping of EEG complexity could serve as a marker for chronic pain severity.

papers.title: Beyond flavor: dietary vanillyl alcohol, a D₂ receptor antagonist promoting sleep.
papers.summary: This study investigated the sleep-promoting effects of dietary vanillyl alcohol (VA) in mouse models, demonstrating that VA significantly prolonged total sleep time and shortened sleep latency via dopamine D2 receptor antagonism and rebalancing of neurotransmitters. The findings support VA as a naturally derived food ingredient for developing sleep-promoting functional foods.

papers.title: Amphetamine-type stimulants in young adults with ADHD: effects on sleep, circadian rhythms, and neuropsychiatric outcomes.
papers.summary: This mini-review synthesizes literature on amphetamine-type stimulant use, sleep, circadian rhythms, and neuropsychiatric outcomes in young adults with ADHD, highlighting how stimulant pharmacology interacts with circadian system and sleep to potentially increase susceptibility to circadian misalignment and sleep disruption.

papers.title: Magnetoreceptive CRY/MagR complexes: linking circadian redox signalling to protein aggregation in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: This review examines magneto-proteins, particularly CRY/MagR-based magnetoreceptor complexes, and their potential intersections with Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease pathology. It synthesizes evidence suggesting these complexes may modulate oxidative stress, mitochondrial bioenergetics, protein aggregation, and circadian control, but notes that direct human validation remains limited.

papers.title: Perioperative transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation and EEG biomarkers of sleep improvement after gynecologic laparoscopy: protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a randomized controlled trial testing whether perioperative transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) reduces postoperative sleep disturbance incidence after gynecologic laparoscopy, with continuous EEG monitoring to explore mechanistic biomarkers.

papers.title: Insomnia Increases Susceptibility to Sciatica: Evidence from Mendelian Randomization and Integrative Genetic Analyses.
papers.summary: Using Mendelian randomization and integrative genetic analyses, this study found a causal effect of insomnia increasing sciatica risk (OR 3.15), with genetic correlation and prioritized candidate genes EIF3KP1 and PPIP5K2, suggesting central nervous system mechanisms.

papers.title: Genetic and stochastic basis of phenotypic discordance in 16p11.2 mouse model deletion.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The study examined phenotypic discordance in a 16p11.2 deletion mouse model, finding that ~50% of isogenic del/+ mice show high seizure susceptibility to pentylenetetrazole. High responders exhibited distinct circuit activation, reduced cortical volume, sleep disturbances, and altered gene expression, suggesting convergent molecular and structural signatures underlying variable expressivity.

papers.title: EEG coherence signatures of sport-specific motor imagery in elite freestyle skiing aerials athletes.
papers.summary: This study characterized EEG coherence during sport-specific motor imagery in elite freestyle skiing aerials athletes. High-difficulty imagery elicited stronger theta-band coherence, and correct judgments were associated with higher high-alpha and theta coherence, suggesting preliminary EEG signatures of motor imagery quality.

papers.title: Development and preliminary evaluation of a Neuman Systems Model-based protocol for postoperative delirium prevention in patients undergoing pancreatic cancer surgery.
papers.summary: The authors developed a Neuman Systems Model-based protocol for postoperative delirium prevention in pancreatic cancer surgery patients via literature review and Delphi process, and tested it in a historical control study. The intervention group showed significantly lower delirium incidence (10.0% vs 26.7%), shorter delirium duration, and better postoperative outcomes including quality of life and psychological scores.

papers.title: The Kairos of the upper airway: The critical time of mid-to-late expiration in the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.summary: This review proposes that the upper airway has a 'Kairos' in late expiration where positive airway pressure therapy must be maintained to optimize pharyngeal patency. It argues that preventing late expiratory narrowing may be more important for airway stability than previously appreciated, based on evidence of smallest airway size and reduced expiratory pressure effects.

papers.title: Εndogenous metabolomic responses in circadian disrupted night shift working populations: a scoping review.
papers.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Center
papers.summary: This scoping review examined human studies on the association between night shift work and endogenous metabolomic responses. Thirteen studies were included, consistently reporting specific metabolites and pathways altered by night shift work, highlighting the potential for metabolomics to link circadian disruption with carcinogenic risk.

papers.title: Hello darkness, my old friend: Electricity loadshedding effects on sleep and studying habits in South African university students.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional online survey of 1124 South African university students during 2023 found that 73% reported loadshedding-affected sleep, with 80% reporting worse sleep, and those with worse sleep more often reported a drop in grades. Access to alternative power was associated with nearly 60% reduced odds of worse sleep.

papers.title: Future goals after clear illustrations of morbidity and mortality associated with wearable-measured short sleep duration.
papers.summary: The abstract is empty, so no summary can be provided based solely on the supplied information. The title suggests a commentary on future goals after clear illustrations of morbidity and mortality associated with wearable-measured short sleep duration.

papers.title: Effects of morning versus evening exercise on sleep: a systematic review of comparative studies with a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.summary: This systematic review with meta-analysis of 18 randomized controlled trials (16 in meta-analysis) found no clear overall advantage of morning versus evening exercise for most sleep outcomes, but evening/nighttime exercise was associated with higher wake after sleep onset (WASO), indicating a modest effect on sleep continuity. Subgroup analyses suggested timing effects were more apparent at higher exercise intensities.

papers.title: Sleep duration and tiredness at school from childhood to adolescence: repeated surveys over 10 years in Swedish schoolchildren.
papers.journal: Journal of research in nursing : JRN
papers.summary: This repeated survey study across 10 years in Swedish schoolchildren found that insufficient sleep prevalence rose from below 10% at ages 6-10 to 31% at age 14 and 74% at age 16, and shorter sleep was associated with increased tiredness at school.

papers.title: Aligning obstructive sleep apnoea care with underlying drivers: A lifestyle-metabolic perspective.
papers.summary: This perspective with targeted evidence synthesis argues for integrating lifestyle and metabolic interventions into routine OSA care, citing evidence that such interventions can reduce OSA severity and cardiometabolic risk, potentially through mechanisms beyond weight loss. It proposes a pragmatic multidisciplinary care model pairing airway therapies with lifestyle modification.

papers.title: Risk Factors for Postoperative Sleep Disturbance in Elderly Patients Undergoing Hip Arthroplasty Surgery: The Role of Preoperative Depression and Anxiety.
papers.summary: This case-control study of 204 elderly hip arthroplasty patients identified preoperative anxiety and depression, postoperative day 1 pain, and longer time to first ambulation as independent risk factors for postoperative sleep disturbance (PSD). Preoperative anxiety and postoperative pain showed a significant synergistic interaction.

papers.title: Perioperative sleep disturbance: A bibliometric analysis.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis mapped research on perioperative sleep disturbance from 2004 to 2024, analyzing 3178 publications from Web of Science and PubMed. The field expanded substantially, with China and the United States as top contributors, and current research focuses on surgery-related sleep problems, pain, sleep quality, melatonin, and postoperative delirium.

papers.title: Fatigue and Driving Safety in Early Parenthood: Developing Feasible Risk-Reduction Strategies Through Co-Design.
papers.journal: Health promotion journal of Australia : official journal of Australian Association of Health Promotion Professionals
papers.summary: Using co-design with 14 parents of young children, this study developed educational resources for fatigued driving in early parenthood, resulting in a website and infographics. Parents emphasized brief materials and feasible strategies, highlighting the need for risk-reduction approaches applicable when sleep and travel control are limited.

papers.title: Effect of Intranasal Dexmedetomidine on the Night Before Surgery for Postoperative Delirium in Older Patients Undergoing Total Hip or Knee Arthroplasty: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.summary: This randomized clinical trial tested intranasal dexmedetomidine (100 μg) administered the night before surgery in 232 older patients undergoing total hip or knee arthroplasty. The intervention reduced postoperative delirium incidence within 3 days (10.3% vs. 20.7%, relative risk = 0.50) and improved perioperative sleep quality, with no severe adverse events.

papers.title: Withdrawal notice to "Corrigendum to Complement activation sustains neuroinflammation and deteriorates adult neurogenesis and spatial memory impairment in rat hippocampus following sleep deprivation" [Brain, Behav., Immun. 137 (2026) 106787].
papers.summary: This is a withdrawal notice for a corrigendum to a previously published article on complement activation and sleep deprivation effects.

papers.title: Social Media Use, Sleep Quality, and Self-Rated Health Among First-Year Students at George Mason University Before and After the COVID-19 Pandemic.
papers.summary: This longitudinal study of 349 first-year university students assessed the relationships between social media use, sleep quality, and self-rated health before and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Poor sleep quality mediated the effects of total social media use on self-rated health both cross-sectionally and longitudinally.

papers.title: Primary Care Providers Journey with OSA Care, Challenges and Strategies: A Qualitative Study.
papers.summary: This qualitative study interviewed 21 primary care providers to create a Journey Map of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) care. It identified barriers (e.g., limited training, unclear roles, low patient engagement) and enablers (e.g., accessible resources, shared screening roles) across five phases of OSA management, with negative emotions during treatment and long-term management phases.

papers.title: Paroxysmal tonic upgaze mimicking epileptic seizures in infancy: a diagnostic challenge.
papers.summary: This case report describes an 11-month-old infant with paroxysmal tonic upgaze, a non-epileptic disorder, highlighting its clinical features and the importance of recognizing it to avoid misdiagnosis of epilepsy.

papers.title: Trajectory Patterns of Perioperative Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms in Patients With Digestive System Malignancies and Their Impact on Postoperative Outcomes.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study of 285 patients with digestive system malignancies identified three distinct perioperative anxiety and depressive symptom trajectories (resilient, recovery, chronic) using latent class growth analysis. The chronic trajectory was associated with higher inflammation markers, more complications, longer hospital stays, and lower recovery quality, with independent predictors including stage III disease and reduced social support.

papers.title: The impact of physical activity on mental health across diverse populations in Saudi Arabia: a narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines the association between physical activity and mental health in Saudi Arabia, noting positive effects on sleep, cognition, and quality of life across diverse populations. It highlights sociocultural, environmental, and social barriers to physical activity and identifies gaps in research, including the need for longitudinal and gender-sensitive interventions.

papers.title: Potential mechanisms of acupuncture in regulating neuroinflammation and central sensitization in chronic pain: a narrative review of preclinical, clinical, and translational evidence.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes preclinical and clinical evidence on acupuncture's potential to modulate neuroinflammation and central sensitization in chronic pain. It reports that acupuncture may regulate spinal glial activation and descending pain pathways, with clinical effects varying by phenotype and measurable via tools like quantitative sensory testing.

papers.title: Machine learning and molecular docking-driven identification of novel umami peptides from pea protein and electroencephalography (EEG) neural mechanisms analysis of their umami-enhancing effects.
papers.summary: This study used machine learning and molecular docking to identify novel umami peptides from pea protein, including QEGEK, QEEEEQSH, and ATTETVDALR. EEG analysis showed that two peptides enhanced umami perception, with stronger neural oscillations in theta, alpha, and beta bands, and activation in parietal and parieto-occipital regions.

papers.title: Education Research: Development of a Workplace-Based Assessment to Enhance EEG Interpretation Skills for Medical Students.
papers.summary: The authors developed a workplace-based assessment (WBA) tool for EEG interpretation during a 2-week medical student elective. Over 79 WBAs with 20 students, they found a significant reduction in faculty assistance needed from week 1 to week 2, and high feasibility and educational value reported by students and faculty.

papers.title: Construction of an e-Health Literacy Program for Patients with Obstructive Sleep Apnea-Hypopnea Syndrome Based on Integrative Model of eHealth Use.
papers.summary: This study developed an eHealth literacy intervention program for patients with obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) using the Integrative Model of eHealth Use and expert validation, resulting in a program with 3 first-level indicators and high expert authority. The program was deemed feasible and scientifically valid.

papers.title: Acupotomy at spinal acupoints for primary insomnia: an exploration of therapeutic effectiveness.
papers.summary: This clinical study compared acupotomy at spinal acupoints versus zolpidem for primary insomnia in 185 patients, finding that acupotomy significantly improved overall response rate, sleep quality, hyperarousal, and neurotransmitter levels, with fewer adverse reactions.

papers.title: A network meta-analysis of commercial Chinese polyherbal preparations for insomnia in the elderly: focusing on sleep quality and the neuro-immune axis.
papers.summary: This network meta-analysis of 19 RCTs (1851 elderly participants) found that commercial Chinese polyherbal preparations combined with conventional therapy most effectively reduced PSQI scores and improved clinical response in geriatric insomnia, with exploratory evidence suggesting reduced serum IL-6.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
